messages:
Elena Morris: Heads-up — Kestrel Labs wants to run a short POC to migrate from PromptlyAI. They care mostly about parity for our text-to-structured responses, encryption/KMS, and pricing for reserved capacity. Can we map blockers and an ask list?
Samir Patel: Got it. quick Qs: do they need VPC/private deployment or is Dedicated + contract enough?
Elena Morris: Prefer Dedicated with VPC peering + customer-managed KMS. Enterprise legal flagged data residency (EU) and SOC2 evidence.
Maya Chen: @Elena put the security checklist below. we'll need answers for KMS key import, HSM support, audit log retention, and pen test reports. also request for SSO SCIM/SCIM groups.
Elena Morris: copying Kestrel's two big blockers from their email: 1) exact behavior parity for the /generate endpoint (stop tokens, sampling seed), 2) billing granularity for sub-route metering.
Owen Ruiz: For parity we should propose a small test harness — their top 50 prompts + canonical prompt transformations. Acceptance criteria: 95% identical intent + <5% increase in hallucination rate vs baseline.
Samir Patel: Agree. I'll draft a POC plan: - ingest 50 prompts - run on PromptlyAI baseline and Redwood models (r-xlarge, r-quant) - diff for tokenization + stop token handling - sample seeds where applicable - spot check top-10 intents
Elena Morris: Can you also include a small signal test for streaming vs non-streaming responses? they complained about slight truncation when switching to streams.
Samir Patel: Yep. will include stream/nonstream parity. Will note KV cache warm vs cold behavior too.
Maya Chen: Security notes for the POC environment: no customer data in plaintext logs, ephemeral KMS keys for POC, and VPC peering only from their static IPs. Send them our SOC2 cert + latest pen-test summary once legal signs NDA.
Elena Morris: Legal already got a one-way NDA signed but they want a more detailed data processing addendum. I'll ping legal.
Owen Ruiz: Pricing ask from Kestrel: they want an up-front committed tier for Dedicated (3 months min), and a migration credit if they bring parity traffic within 30 days. How flexible are we on migration credits?
Samir Patel: We can do a one-time onboarding credit for verified parity runs. amount TBD — propose $Xk equivalent to 1 month of expected committed spend. Need finance approval.
Elena Morris: They also asked about rate limits: PromptlyAI allowed 100 rps per API key. Kestrel needs sustained 40 rps with bursts to 150. Are our Dedicated pools able to guarantee that?
Owen Ruiz: Yes for Dedicated with reserved capacity and proper autoscaling/burst configured. We'll document expected latency percentiles. Samir can add a perf run.
Samir Patel: I'll run a short perf smoke on dev to show 95th p50/p95 numbers for their expected payload sizes. will post curl snippet and logs.
Samir Patel: (snippet)
```
# example compare curl
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"r-xlarge","input":"${PROMPT}","stop":["\\n\\n"],"stream":false}'
```
Samir Patel: Note: PromptlyAI uses a different tokenization for special chars; include a token-diff step in the harness.
Maya Chen: Security follow-up: we'll need to answer their vendor questionnaire items: encryption at rest (AES-256), in-transit (TLS1.3), key rotation window, and whether we support customer-supplied keys (yes via KMS integration). Also provide contact for incident response.
Elena Morris: Kestrel also wants a short runbook for fallback: if our model variant shows regression, they'd like automatic fallback to a compatible variant of the same family and webhooks for failure events. Can we commit to that for the POC window?
Owen Ruiz: We can configure fallback policies and webhooks for Dedicated. Will add that to the POC config doc.
devops-bot: deploy-notify: New ephemeral POC cluster ready in eu-west-1; creds will be rotated and posted to the secure vault. :white_check_mark:
Samir Patel: Perfect. timeline proposal: Day 0-2: environment/network setup + KMS exchange. Day 3-6: ingest prompts + run baseline vs our models. Day 7-9: analyze diffs, security review, and parity sign-off.
Maya Chen: I'll prepare a short security appendix for the POC with required evidence and contact points.
Elena Morris: Owners: Samir (POC plan + perf), Maya (security questionnaire + DPA), Owen (fallback/runbook + infra), Elena (customer comms + pricing ask). I'll draft an email to Kestrel with this plan and next steps.
Owen Ruiz: One more thing — add an acceptance test for stop-token handling where they send nested markers like "<<END>>" and ensure we match behavior. Those edgecases caused most of their prior regressions.
Samir Patel: noted. will include a tiny unit in harness to reproduce.
Elena Morris: thanks all. I'll send the email after legal confirms DPA timeline. :thumbsup:
Owen Ruiz: :eyes: keep me posted if legal stalls — we can propose a limited-scope DPA addendum for the POC only.
Maya Chen: +1. let's not block the POC while we sort full enterprise DPA. temporary mitigations are fine.
Elena Morris: Closing thread for now — will reopen after I hear from legal.
